title: Duracell Coppertop AA vs Rayovac Ultra Pro AA

brand.product: Duracell Coppertop Duralock AA LR6 alkaline, 4-pack retail card (MN1500B4)

summary: Both are 1.5 V AA alkaline cells with a stated 10-year shelf life from the same shop, and the Rayovac 24-pack costs 78% less per cell.
evidence: Both product pages read on batteryjunction.com on 14 November 2026: Duracell USD 7.15 for 4 (USD 1.79 a cell, no reduction shown) and Rayovac USD 9.45 for 24 (39 cents a cell, a sale price; regular USD 10.50, which is still 76% less per cell). Duracell's page gives alkaline, 1.5 V, LR6 and a 10-year shelf life; Rayovac's gives alkaline, 1.5 V and a 10-year shelf life (85% of its life kept after 10 years).
differences: The Rayovac is a 24-cell contractor pack, so you spend more at the checkout. Duracell sells the same MN1500 cell in bulk boxes at Battery Junction too, which is cheaper than the 4-card. No test we read compares these two.
why: Same size, chemistry, voltage and stated shelf life, at under a quarter of the price per cell if you can use 24.

title: Duracell CR2032 vs Panasonic CR2032

brand.product: Duracell Duralock CR2032 3V lithium coin cell, 4-pack retail card (DL2032B4PK)

alternative.product: Panasonic CR2032 3V lithium coin cell, single on a tear strip

summary: Both are 3 V CR2032 lithium manganese dioxide coin cells from the same shop, and the Panasonic costs 71% less per cell. Duracell adds a bitter coating; Panasonic's page doesn't mention one.
evidence: Both product pages read on batteryjunction.com on 14 November 2026, both at sale prices: Duracell USD 6.21 for 4 (USD 1.55 a cell; regular USD 6.90) and Panasonic USD 0.45 each (regular USD 0.50, a 71% gap too). Both pages give lithium, LiMnO2, 3 V. Duracell's states 225 mAh and Panasonic's 220 mAh and a 5-year shelf life. Several of these prices are Battery Junction's Black Friday sale prices, so they may rise again.
differences: Duracell's listing mentions a bitter coating to discourage children from swallowing the cell; Panasonic's comes loose on a tear strip with no coating mentioned. Panasonic's page shows two different UPCs, so we left its barcode off.
why: Any CR2032 fits a key fob, scale or motherboard. Buy the Duracell if small children are around, for the bitter coating; otherwise the Panasonic is the same cell type at under a third of the price.
